entries.title: DHS purpose and service relationships
entries.facts: DHS works with counties, Tribal Nations, communities and providers to support Minnesotans' health, independence and life in community. Its public participation channels include meetings, comment opportunities and advisory bodies.
entries.application: Map the affected people, service partners and decision owners before proposing a change. Public participation is a source of knowledge about service experience.

entries.title: DHS organizational responsibilities
entries.facts: The agency directory lists Aging and Disability Services, Behavioral Health, Health Care, and Homelessness, Housing and Support Services. Cross-agency functions include finance, compliance, legal counsel, inspector general, strategy and performance, employee culture, equity and inclusion, communications, and MNIT.
entries.application: Use the function responsible for the question. A division name alone does not establish authority over every step of a service.

entries.title: Where Disability Services sits
entries.facts: The agency directory and CBSM introduction place Disability Services within Aging and Disability Services. DSD manages publicly funded supports for people with developmental or physical disabilities, chronic medical conditions, and acquired or traumatic brain injuries. DSD is not the DHS Licensing function; DHS retaining a license category does not mean DSD administers that license.
entries.application: Separate DSD program expertise from licensing, billing and individual lead-agency responsibilities.

entries.title: DHS strategic direction and staff culture
entries.facts: The published 2023–2027 plan has three outcomes: Minnesotans thrive, people experience high-quality services, and DHS employees thrive in an inclusive environment. Its goals address equitable access, community choice, caregiving capacity, service quality, program integrity, partnerships, inclusion, psychological safety and career growth. It also addresses continuity during agency separation.
entries.application: Connect a recommendation to a concrete staff or service outcome. Identify the experience to improve, an observable measure and the work that can be simplified.

entries.title: County and Tribal partnerships
entries.facts: County Relations supports DHS relationships with Minnesota's 87 counties. The Office of Indian Policy coordinates consultation with Tribal governments. Lead-agency reviews examine HCBS administration and outcomes and inform improvements.
entries.application: Include county operational knowledge where relevant. Government-to-government consultation and community engagement have different participants and purposes; identify the appropriate Office of Indian Policy route for formal Tribal consultation.

entries.title: DSD priorities and person-centered outcomes
entries.facts: DSD's published priorities cover community participation; health, wellness and safety; a home of one's choosing; enduring relationships; control of supports; and work and income. Its goals address access, timely service, quality, partnership, innovation and person-centered decisions. The introduction displays an old review date, so it does not establish current internal targets.
entries.application: Use the person's own goals and preferences to frame alternatives. Assess burden, accessibility, continuity and opportunities for self-direction.

entries.title: Finding DSD policy and operational guidance
entries.facts: The CBSM organizes assessment, support planning, case management, safeguards, eligibility, employment, service options and waiver guidance. It distinguishes BI, CAC, CADI, DD and Elderly Waiver topics. The LTSS policy directory links additional manuals for CDCS, EIDBI, Moving Home Minnesota and other programs.
entries.application: Start with the specific service and current manual page. A directory is a route to policy, not proof of an individual's eligibility or a particular rate.

entries.title: MnCHOICES assessment and support planning
entries.facts: MnCHOICES supports long-term services and supports assessment and planning by counties, Tribal Nations and managed care organizations. DHS coordinates related updates through aging, disability and MnCHOICES communication channels. The CBSM provides case-management policy guidance. MNIT provides technology support; managed care organizations use MnCHOICES in care coordination. Using the application does not establish responsibility for system administration.
entries.application: For an assessment-process change, distinguish policy, the person's support-planning experience, lead-agency workflow and application support. Use those distinctions to identify collaborators.

entries.title: Person-centered planning across partners
entries.facts: DHS's person-centered, informed choice and transition protocol addresses support planning by counties, Tribal organizations and managed care organizations. HCBS settings oversight includes provider enrollment, case management and licensing.
entries.application: Ask how the proposed change affects meaningful choice, community participation and continuity. Trace the effect across planning, provider practice and oversight.

entries.title: CFSS and the transition from PCA and CSG
entries.facts: Community First Services and Supports offers flexible home and community support options and replaces personal care assistance and the Consumer Support Grant. DHS directs lead agencies to the CFSS Manual for transition guidance.
entries.application: Use the current transition manual for deadlines and individual circumstances. Explain the service change in accessible language and identify the person's lead-agency contact.

entries.title: Disability Waiver Program changes
entries.facts: The new Disability Waiver Program site describes a simpler structure, individual budgets and online tools. At the September 8 review, it said implementation timing was still being determined. It provides resources, community input and Advisory Task Force on Waiver Reimagine routes.
entries.application: Separate planned changes from rules already in effect. Use the official update page before giving a launch date, and connect communications to the affected people and partners.

entries.title: Disability Waiver Rate System
entries.facts: DHS's Disability Waiver Rate System page provides rate-setting guidance and 2026 remediation updates. Current policy for the Rate Management System is linked through the CBSM.
entries.application: Locate the exact service, effective period and authoritative rate guidance. Do not turn a general organizational summary into a rate calculation.

entries.title: Employment First and E1MN
entries.facts: Employment First prioritizes competitive, integrated work. E1MN connects DHS, the Department of Employment and Economic Development and the Department of Education. DHS links employment exploration, development and support services, benefits-planning tools and lead-agency employment liaisons.
entries.application: Map school-to-work, vocational rehabilitation, waiver support and benefits-planning handoffs. The person's employment goals determine the starting point.

entries.title: HCBS licensing versus enrollment and service planning
entries.facts: DHS licenses certain home and community-based services under chapter 245D. Its licensing page distinguishes licensure from MHCP enrollment. It describes a licensing moratorium beginning January 1, 2026, anticipated through December 31, 2027, with a lead-agency-based exception process.
entries.application: Verify the current exception criteria and process before advising a provider. Keep licensing, Medicaid enrollment and individual service authorization distinct.

entries.title: Complex transitions back to community
entries.facts: DHS's Complex Transitions Team connects expertise for people facing barriers moving from hospital or institutional settings to community. Its technical assistance supplements existing processes; hospitals first work with the person's lead agency.
entries.application: Identify the barrier, lead agency, hospital and needed expertise. Support preparation and navigation without claiming a referral has been sent or a requirement waived.

entries.title: DSD contacts and Disability Hub MN
entries.facts: DHS's division directory lists DSD at 651-431-4300 or 866-267-7655 and Disability Hub MN at 866-333-2466. The Hub helps people navigate services and options. DSD competitive grants are a separate route from an individual's request for service assistance.
entries.application: Choose the service-navigation or grant route according to the actual request. Recheck phone numbers before relying on an older reference.

entries.title: DSD competitive grants and funding opportunities
entries.facts: DSD's grants FAQ links current opportunities and explains that eligibility, deadlines and submission instructions belong to each RFP. It also provides a grants contact form and an online grant-management route.
entries.application: Help compare requirements, develop accessible proposals and track deliverables. Do not infer an open funding opportunity from an older award announcement.

entries.title: Civil rights and equal service access
entries.facts: DHS describes equal access responsibilities across the department, county human-services agencies and providers. Its civil-rights contact handles service discrimination complaints, information, records, liaison work and training through Equal Opportunity and Access.
entries.application: Distinguish learning or process improvement from a person seeking the complaint route. Provide the relevant published contact without making a formal finding.

entries.title: Language access and translated information
entries.facts: DHS publishes language-access resources and translated program documents to support access to information and benefits.
entries.application: Identify the audience's requested languages and communication needs, the document owner and the appropriate translation or interpretation support. Do not infer an individual's language needs from identity.

entries.title: Finance, appeals and data requests
entries.facts: DHS's operations directory separates financial operations, appeals, privacy information and data requests. Financial operations includes budgets, payments and payroll support. Appeals concerns disputed benefits, services or other program decisions.
entries.application: Route by the actual issue: a benefits appeal, a public data request and an internal budget question require different processes.

entries.title: Staff development, technology and communication
entries.facts: The directory lists development and learning, human resources and workforce planning within Employee Culture. Communications supports public and media information. MNIT supplies information infrastructure, application services and technology coordination.
entries.application: For staff-facing changes, identify learning, workforce, communication and technology dependencies. Confirm the internal process owner rather than inventing a reporting line.

entries.title: Behavioral health and coordinated care
entries.facts: DHS's CCBHC materials describe integration of mental-health and substance-use services and care coordination. They distinguish service requirements, Medicaid coverage, licensing and background-study responsibilities, and include implementation updates.
entries.application: For a cross-service initiative, separate care continuity, program policy and provider requirements. Consult dated updates before asserting an implementation deadline.

entries.title: DHS and DCYF boundaries
entries.facts: DCYF's public site covers child care, child support, child safety, family supports, food and cash assistance, and youth services. DHS's June 2025 bulletin transferred specified child-care and child-foster-care licensing functions to DCYF, while retaining other categories including HCBS and children's residential facilities.
entries.application: Route by program and license type, not just the age of the people served. A child-related question does not automatically belong to DCYF.
units: Department of Children, Youth, and Families

entries.title: DHS and Direct Care and Treatment boundaries
entries.facts: DCT's 2026 fact sheet states that Direct Care and Treatment became a standalone agency on July 1, 2025.
entries.application: Treat state-operated treatment responsibilities as a distinct agency relationship. DSD and DCT are different organizations.

entries.title: Minnesota Health Care Programs and Medicaid
entries.facts: MHCP includes Medical Assistance, MinnesotaCare and the Minnesota Family Planning Program. DHS works with county and Tribal workers and other partners on eligibility and enrollment. Depending on the program, delivery uses fee-for-service providers or contracted managed care organizations.
entries.application: Identify coverage, enrollment, billing and care-delivery questions separately. A change to one part of this process may affect other partners.

entries.title: Housing and homelessness relationships
entries.facts: DHS's housing work connects housing, services and income supports so people can live in their chosen communities.
entries.application: Distinguish housing availability, income support and service coordination. Verify current program availability before suggesting a specific benefit.

entries.title: Aging services and community support
entries.facts: DHS works with providers and community organizations on home and community-based supports for older adults, needs assessment and training. Its aging overview points people to Minnesota Aging Pathways and related community resources.
entries.application: Connect aging and disability supports where needs overlap, while preserving the specific program's eligibility and operational routes.

entries.title: Tribal and Urban Indian Relations
entries.facts: DHS describes Tribal and Urban Indian Relations as supporting consultation and program development with Tribal governments. Its published focus includes sovereignty relationships, infrastructure, access, disparities, culturally appropriate programs and fiscal resources.
entries.application: Identify the relevant Tribal government or urban Indian organization based on the work. They are not interchangeable, and an organization does not represent every individual.

entries.title: Adult protection and reporting routes
entries.facts: DHS Adult Protection provides policy, training, consultation and data work and operates the Minnesota Adult Abuse Reporting Center. The overview links reporting guidance for the public and mandated reporters.
entries.application: Provide the published reporting route when someone seeks it; preparation or learning in this program does not submit a report.

entries.title: Legislation, budgets and evidence
entries.facts: DHS legislative staff work with lawmakers on proposals, reports and budget topics. The department publishes session fact sheets, legislative reports and background materials.
entries.application: Distinguish a proposal from enacted law and an appropriation from an open grant. Use the relevant report and effective date when explaining a change.

gaps.detail: Public sources do not establish current DSD internal teams, informal working relationships, delegated decision authority, or the pilot's internal sponsor and operational contacts.
gaps.resolution: Add Gary's role-based relationship map and authorized internal materials when available. No private staff directory was inferred.

gaps.detail: The older DSD About us page says Continuing Care Administration; the agency directory and CBSM introduction say Aging and Disability Services.
gaps.resolution: Use the corroborated Aging and Disability Services placement; retain the legacy source as historical evidence, not current structure.

gaps.detail: The agencywide directory and older executive biographies differ on Aging and Disability Services leadership. The directory contains vacancies and interim appointments.
gaps.resolution: Use role-based routing. Recheck the live directory for person-specific questions; no permanent officeholder list is embedded.

gaps.detail: The agencywide public page presents the 2023–2027 plan. A 2026 capital-budget document labels a different set of treatment-oriented goals 2026–2028.
gaps.resolution: Keep the agencywide plan and capital-budget document distinct. Do not silently replace one with the other.

gaps.detail: PartnerLink and internal operational systems may require authorized access. Public source research does not establish access to their contents.
gaps.resolution: Use public manuals and directory routes now; add authorized internal material with its actual access scope.
